summary: Attribute translation error causing GCP->AWS role chaining to drop environment tag during deploys
description:
Issue summary: A subset of service account session exchanges from GCP Workload Identity Federation to AWS STS are losing the 'env' session tag during attribute translation. Impact: Automated deploys (ops/deploy-runner) that rely on env tag for permission scoping are failing with AccessDenied when trying to create ephemeral resources. Scope: Intermittent (~3% of deploy attempts) since credential rotation window started on 2026-03-09.

Observed behavior: Requests that chain GCP->AWS assume-role return a valid STS token but the session-tags payload received by downstream services lacks the `env` attribute, causing permission boundary evaluation to deny actions. Errors seen in deploy-runner logs are AccessDenied: action denied by permission boundary evaluation.

Expected behavior: Attribute translation should preserve and pass through the `env` session tag (e.g., env=prod) so that AWS assume-role sessions inherit the correct scoping.

Impact assessment: Affects internal CI/CD deploy path for multiple teams using cross-cloud deployer. No customer-facing outages reported, but internal deploy cadence degraded; rollout blocked for some hotfixes.

Workaround: Manual assume-role using long-lived ops role or re-run deploy with explicit --force-env tag provided (not ideal). Mitigation applied: temporary tag-normalizer bypass in auth-proxy for queue deployments to restore deploys while fix is developed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a standard deploy on ops/deploy-runner in prod (us-east) that uses GCP Workload Identity Federation to assume an AWS role.
2) Observe the STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity flow in auth-proxy logs and capture session tags payload sent to AWS.
3) Inspect downstream permission-evaluation logs in iam-audit; some sessions will be missing the 'env' key and result in AccessDenied when performing resource:create actions.
4) Re-run the same job repeatedly; issue reproduces intermittently (~1 in 30 runs during window).
comments: Aisha Patel (reporter) - 2026-03-11: Raised after oncall reported two failed hotfix deploys; attach auth-proxy traces and initial logs.

Tom Nguyen (assignee) - 2026-03-11: Triage done; initial hypothesis is attribute-mapper in the auth-proxy is dropping tags when the incoming token contains both `x-goog-attrs` and `custom-env` header. Reproduced locally once.
SRE Oncall (Dan Brooks) - 2026-03-12: Applied temporary bypass in auth-proxy to preserve raw attributes for deploy queue only. Deploys back to green for opsteam. Not a permanent fix.
Infra Eng (Lina Moreno) - 2026-03-12: Noted a recent library bump in workload-identity-client (v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0) that changed attribute normalization rules; adding to investigation stack.
Tom Nguyen - 2026-03-13: Patch prepared for tag-normalizer edge case; running canary in staging now. Will schedule prod deploy after validation and security review.
Security (Rajiv Singh) - 2026-03-13: Reviewed patch; no new privileges requested. Ensure audit log retention for affected time window is extended to 90 days.
Tom Nguyen - 2026-03-13: Monitoring metrics: deploy success rate increased from 97% -> 99.6% after bypass. Still seeing 0.2% residual failures unrelated to tag-drop (investigating separately).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Workload-identity-client v2.5.0 introduced attribute dedup that prefers header keys over payload keys; in some orders env tag is deduped out.
Hypothesis 2: An upstream load-balancer rewrite for internal header `x-rw-attrs` reorders keys leading to non-deterministic merge behavior in the auth-proxy's normalizer.

Trace: Captured 18 failing sessions; 16 of 18 had request header `x-goog-assertion-attrs` followed by `x-rw-attrs`. When headers arrive in that order, normalizer returned attributes map without 'env'.
Repro script: ops/tools/repro-env-tag-flaky.sh reproduces failure deterministically by toggling header order — suggests normalization bug rather than network loss.

Code pointers: auth-proxy/pkg/attrs/normalizer.go: the mergeAttrs function uses map iteration order from parsed JSON which can be non-deterministic. Should use deterministic merge with explicit precedence rules.
Security check: No token forgery or privilege escalation observed; only attribute mapping loss leading to stricter permission boundary denial.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: bypass in auth-proxy that skips normalization for deploy-queue traffic deployed 2026-03-12. Permanent fix: deterministic merge ordering and unit tests added (PR #1221). Pending full rollout to prod after canary validation and security review. Extended audit retention for window. Follow-up: ensure library upgrade policy includes attribute-normalization integration test.
suggested_followups: 1) Full prod rollout of PR #1221 after 48h canary with no regressions.
2) Add header-order fuzz tests to workload-identity-client test suite.
3) Update runbook to include quick bypass steps for tag-normalizer failures.
4) Postmortem within 7 days with timeline and action owners (owner: Tom Nguyen).
